newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina okays pension investments in equities.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina okays pension investments in equities.

text.p: South Carolina residents overwhelmingly approved a measure to allow the state to invest pension fund money in equities, a state election official said Wednesday.
With a margin of 73 percent, 479,214 voters said yes to the constitutional amendment and 180,199 said no, Julie Lybrand, public information officer for the state election commission, said.
"This is a dramatic step forward for South Carolina," said Scott Malyerck, a spokesman for the state treasurer. "We can earn so much more for South Carolina."
The state pension fund has about $14 billion under management and is one of only a handful of states that cannot buy equities, Malyerck said.
Before lifting the 100-year-old ban on equities, the pension fund was investing only in government securities, Malyerck said.
The legislation will now draft legislation to carry out the mandate, he said.
